papers.title_en: SENRI: Understanding the Space-Event Nexus in Real-Life Videos
papers.authors: Kehan Lan, Kaining Ying, Henghui Ding, Kaipeng Zhang
papers.evidence: 长视频中空间与事件的记忆及检索问答
papers.tldr: 现有长视频理解很少建模事件与空间的关联，SENRI在约25.3小时连续第一视角视频上定义空间—事件双向任务，并构建500道人工标注选择题。评测显示直接感知、证据检索与持久记忆三类范式均表现不佳，暴露证据缺口。作者提出SENRI-Agent，以目标引导视觉核验调度并行验证器并整合工作记忆。该工作为真实生活第一视角理解提供了新基准与改进方向。
papers.abstract_en: Human memories are organized in a way that connects events with their corresponding spatial contexts. An AI assistant should also be able to memorize and recall the nexus of events and spaces. Thus we introduce SENRI, a task that studies this space--event connection in long, continuous real-life egocentric video. It contains six task types in two directions: Event$\rightarrow$Space, which recovers spatial knowledge from event cues, and Space$\rightarrow$Event, which retrieves events from regions and trajectories. To evaluate this, we build SENRI-Bench, containing 500 manually annotated multiple-choice questions over 10 uninterrupted self-recorded videos with around 25.3 hours of content. Also, we evaluate three typical long video understanding paradigms: direct perception, evidence seeking, and persistent memory. The task remains challenging across all three paradigms, highlighting substantial room for improvement. Then we show two representative failure modes of existing memory methods and address these evidence gaps with SENRI-Agent, a controller that uses Target-Guided Visual Check (TGVC) to propose local visual check tasks for parallel verifiers and integrate the reports into a working memory to help with reasoning. Built upon existing memory systems, SENRI-Agent improves the performance of existing baselines without modifying their stored memories. We hope SENRI will provide valuable insights into how real-life egocentric understanding should be evaluated, reveal the gaps in existing approaches, and offer a possible direction for improvement.

papers.authors: Huachen Gao, Yang Yang, Xiaoqian Liang, Xingyu Chen, Youjia Zhang, Qi Zhang, Baorui Ma, Anpei Chen, Wei Yang
papers.evidence: 以表面感知位置编码将图像块令牌锚定到三维表面几何
papers.tldr: 现有多视角Transformer的几何位置编码多基于相机视锥或射线深度，只描述 token 从何处被观测，忽略其所描绘表面的几何。HRoPE 将每个 patch 的局部几何建模为倾斜3D平面，并把平面诱导的 token 级单应变换作为相对位置注入注意力。在 RealEstate10K、CO3Dv2、DL3DV 上，最佳变体持续优于现有几何位置编码。该工作把位置编码从传感器中心推进到表面感知，为跨视角特征对齐提供几何先验。
papers.abstract_en: Geometric Relative Positional Encoding has become the primary mechanism for injecting spatial inductive biases into multi-view transformers. Existing designs condition attention on camera-level frustums or ray-marched depth, associating cross-view tokens through the sensor geometry. Such sensor-centric formulations, however, describe only where a token is observed from, leaving the rich surface geometry of the scene region depicted by the token. In this paper, we advocate a shift toward surface-aware positional encoding that explicitly grounds patch tokens in the geometry of physical surfaces. We introduce HRoPE, which represents the local geometry of each patch as a slanted 3D plane, following the slanted support-window assumption of classical multi-view stereo. We inject token-level, plane-induced homographies into attention as relative transformations. This equips the transformer with a geometric prior for rectifying perspective distortions and aligning patch features across viewpoints. Our encoding requires no ground-truth geometry: the plane parameters can be predicted end-to-end under a view-synthesis objective alone, or derived from foundation models. Extensive experiments on RealEstate10K, CO3Dv2, and DL3DV show that our best variant of HRoPE consistently outperforms the evaluated geometric positional encodings for novel view synthesis. Extensive ablations and analysis show the effectiveness of the proposed encoding. Please refer to our project page at: https://gaohchen.github.io/HRoPE

papers.title_en: GazeLens for Efficient Egocentric Video Question Answering with Simple Gaze-Driven Adaptive Token Reduction
papers.authors: Trong-Thang Pham, Anh Nguyen, Hien Van Nguyen, Ngan Le
papers.evidence: 结合帧选择与注视及问题引导的令牌压缩以保留有限视频证据
papers.tldr: 智能眼镜需在有限算力下用小型视觉语言模型理解用户活动与环境，但冗余帧挤占视觉预算，过度空间压缩又会丢失关键细节。GazeLens 先用 HOG 变化与图像清晰度选帧，再对每帧以高斯池化生成注视聚焦与互补摘要，并由轻量门控结合问题融合为主 token，配合全局场景 token。在 StreamGaze 上，其宏/微准确率优于全网格与 token 缩减基线，且输入前向 FLOPs 更低。
papers.abstract_en: Smart glasses can help users understand their activities and surroundings, but small vision-language models must preserve useful evidence within limited computation. This is difficult because redundant frames consume the visual budget, while aggressive spatial compression can discard relevant details. Although gaze identifies the wearer's focus, the question may require evidence from the surrounding scene. To address these constraints, we propose GazeLens, which combines frame selection with gaze- and question-guided token reduction. First, HOG transitions and image sharpness select frames before visual encoding. For each selected frame, Gaussian pooling then forms gaze-focused and complementary summaries. Because their relevance depends on the question, a lightweight gate blends them into a primary token. Together with a global scene token, this retains both focused and contextual summaries within two tokens per frame. On StreamGaze, GazeLens achieves higher macro and micro accuracy than the evaluated full-grid and token-reduction baselines, with lower input-forward FLOPs than the shared-backbone token-reduction baselines.

papers.title_en: UniRAP: Towards Unified Part-level Physical Affordance Reasoning and Actionable Perception
papers.authors: Linfei Li, Ruining Hu, Lin Zhang, Zhong Wang, Fengyi Zhang, Ying Shen, Binqiang Wang, Xin Zhang
papers.evidence: 统一视觉语言模型将指令映射为可操作几何表示
papers.tldr: 针对视觉语言感知难以将高层语义落到部件级物理交互的问题，UniRAP将部件可供性推理与语言指令到可操作几何映射统一为条件多模态生成任务。模型借助统一接口token融合视觉、文本与可选提示，并用统一可供性解码器联合完成目标检测、部件级可供性分割和4-DoF交互位姿估计。课程式迁移训练从通用视觉解析逐步过渡到交互感知，提升有限文本标注下的数据效率。实验在指代分割、可供性接地和交互位姿估计上取得SOTA，并在动态视频中保持较强时空一致性。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language perception has achieved impressive progress in aligning natural language with visual observations, yet grounding high-level semantics into part-level physical interaction remains challenging. To address this gap, we propose UniRAP, a unified model for inferring part-level physical affordances and mapping language instructions to actionable geometric representations. UniRAP formulates this problem as a conditional multimodal generation task, integrating visual inputs, textual instructions, and optional prompts into a shared spatiotemporal representation space through a unified interface token mechanism. To predict executable contact geometry, we introduce a Unified Affordance Decoder (UAD), which jointly performs object detection, part-level affordance segmentation, and 4-DoF interaction pose estimation by leveraging intermediate segmentation features. In addition, we propose a curriculum-based transfer training strategy that progressively adapts the model from general visual parsing to interaction-aware perception, improving data efficiency under limited textual annotations. Experiments show that UniRAP achieves state-of-the-art performance on referring expression segmentation, affordance grounding, and interaction pose estimation, while maintaining strong spatiotemporal consistency in dynamic video scenarios. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of UniRAP as a unified perception framework for language-guided physical manipulation.

papers.authors: Bavesh Balaji, Pranav Gopinath, Pouya Sadeghi, Sirisha Rambhatla
papers.evidence: 可被查询引导且自适应预算的视觉令牌压缩与分配
papers.tldr: 现有视觉与视觉语言模型通常与查询无关地编码图像，并为每个输入分配固定视觉 token 预算，忽略不同查询所需证据和容量差异。QART 作为骨干无关模块，从冻结编码器特征出发循环构建紧凑表示，并依据查询相关视觉支持上的重建质量动态分配 token，直到保真度足够。在 Visual7W 与 VQAv2 上，仅约 29 个视觉 token 即达 81.96% 和 76.37% 准确率，token 数较密集 VLM 输入减少 20–25 倍。这表明视觉表示的内容与容量都可按查询自适应，而非固定不变。
papers.abstract_en: Visual information worth extracting from an image and the token budget it warrants depend on the text query. Yet modern vision and vision-language models largely encode images independently of the query and allocate a fixed visual token budget to every input. We introduce the Query-Adaptive Recurrent Tokenizer (QART), a backbone-agnostic module that makes visual representations both query-steerable and budget-adaptive. QART steers the visual representation toward query-relevant evidence while adapting its token budget to the amount of information required. Its key principle is simple. Additional tokens are allocated until the visual features relevant to the query are represented with sufficient fidelity. Starting from frozen encoder features, QART recurrently constructs a compact representation and uses reconstruction quality over the query-relevant visual support to control token allocation. On Visual7W and VQAv2, QART achieves 81.96% and 76.37% accuracy using only about 29 visual tokens, reducing token counts by 20-25x relative to dense VLM inputs. It further reaches 92.0% P@1 on CORE and 36.3% PR-AUC on PODS, outperforming SteerViT on PODS by 8.4%. Together, these results show that visual representations need not be fixed in either content or capacity and can instead adapt to what each query requires.

papers.title_en: LonGaussian: Tracking Foundation Priors for Long-Context Feedforward Gaussian Reconstruction
papers.authors: Zhoufeng Xie, Guanjun Wu, Shuai Zhang, Xinggang Wang, Wenyu Liu
papers.evidence: 面向长图像序列的流式前馈高斯重建，控制显存与冗余
papers.tldr: 长视频高保真可渲染3D重建对机器人感知很重要，但现有前馈高斯方法扩展到长序列时面临显存瓶颈与重复表示问题。LonGaussian以预训练流式重建骨干解码长上下文几何特征，并在分块内利用多帧点轨迹合并重复高斯、用渲染深度一致性过滤跨块遮挡。在DL3DV和RealEstate10K上，它提升新视角渲染质量，同时显著减少高斯数量。该工作为长序列前馈高斯重建提供了紧凑且全局可渲染的流式方案。
papers.abstract_en: Reconstructing high-quality, renderable 3D scenes from long videos is essential for robotic perception and embodied intelligence. Many feed-forward Gaussian reconstruction methods rapidly predict 3D scenes from a small set of images, but extending them to longer sequences presents two bottlenecks: jointly processing all views increases GPU memory requirements, while accumulating pixel-aligned predictions redundantly represents the same surfaces and increases storage and rendering costs. We present LonGaussian, a streaming feed-forward framework that reconstructs compact, globally renderable Gaussian scenes from long image sequences with known intrinsics and unknown camera poses. Built on a pretrained streaming 3D reconstruction backbone, LonGaussian decodes long-context geometric features into dense Gaussians. Within each chunk, multi-frame point tracks link repeated observations of the same surface and guide a learned merger to consolidate the corresponding Gaussian predictions. Rendered-depth consistency filtering further suppresses Gaussians from other chunks that incorrectly occlude locally reconstructed surfaces. On DL3DV and RealEstate10K benchmarks, LonGaussian improves novel-view rendering quality while using substantially fewer Gaussians than the evaluated feed-forward baselines.

papers.title_en: Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models
papers.authors: Yuze He, Bin Tan, Zelin Gao, Yujun Shen, Yong-Jin Liu, Nan Xue, Yinghao Xu
papers.evidence: 持久化平面三维记忆条件化后续视频片段
papers.tldr: 视频世界模型在长序列生成中需要持久3D记忆，但逐像素点云存储昂贵且缺乏结构。PPMem以每基元仅7参数的定向平面作为持久记忆，在视频扩散Transformer中加入平面预测头与Depth Token Fusion，自回归联合生成RGB与平面几何并融合成场景记忆，用渲染深度条件后续片段。在DL3DV与RealEstate10K上，其视频质量优于先前3D世界模型，同时输出米制深度、法线与可导出平面几何，并在数百帧大视角变化下保持连贯。
papers.abstract_en: Video world models that generate and explore environments at scale need a persistent 3D memory of what they have produced. Plane primitives offer a natural candidate: a compact set of oriented planes captures the dominant structural elements (e.g., walls, floors, facades) of indoor and outdoor scenes, while requiring only 7 parameters per primitive. We present PPMem, a video world model that adopts plane primitives as its persistent 3D memory. PPMem augments a video diffusion transformer with a planar prediction head and a Depth Token Fusion (DTF) module: each autoregressive chunk jointly produces RGB video and planar geometry, which merges into a persistent plane memory that conditions subsequent chunks via rendered depth. The resulting memory is three orders of magnitude more compact than per-pixel point clouds (~100K primitives, 5MB for a full scene), geometrically explicit (metric depth, normals, exportable surfaces), cross-view consistent (jointly predicted by the shared backbone), and adaptive (refined by the merging procedure as generation proceeds). On DL3DV and RealEstate10K, PPMem outperforms prior 3D-grounded world models in video quality while jointly producing metric-scale depth, surface normals, and exportable planar geometry, sustaining coherence across hundreds of frames under large viewpoint changes. Project page: https://hyzcluster.github.io/ppmem.

papers.title_en: Think Visually Across Space and Time: Grounded Reasoning for Video Segmentation
papers.authors: Junwei Wen, Deshui Miao, Guangming Lu, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Xin Li, Wenjie Pei
papers.evidence: 为实体引用绑定时间支撑与带时间戳的空间证据
papers.tldr: 视频推理分割需根据隐式描述定位目标并预测掩码轨迹，但纯文本CoT缺乏显式视觉指代，形成视频参考鸿沟。论文提出TCoVP，将实体引用、时间支撑与带时间戳空间证据组织为按时间排序的视频基元推理链。基于TCoVP-SFT-15k与TCoVP-RL-13k进行监督微调和链对齐强化学习，并在五个VRS基准、三种骨干上验证。结果显示该时空接地推理显著提升分割性能，为视频推理提供可解释证据组织方式。
papers.abstract_en: Video Reasoning Segmentation (VRS) requires a model to identify an implicitly described target and predict its pixel-level mask trajectory, while resolving the spatial relations and temporal events that determine the answer. Text-only Chain-of-Thought (CoT) can explain a target choice without making the underlying visual references explicit, leaving a \emph{video reference gap} between linguistic inference and the evidence distributed across frames. We introduce \textbf{Temporal Chain of Video Primitives (TCoVP)}, a spatiotemporally grounded form of Video CoT that organizes query-relevant observations into a chronological reasoning chain. Each primitive associates an entity reference with temporal support and timestamped spatial evidence, and the chain interleaves these references with language to guide reasoning about which entity is relevant, when the queried event holds, and where its evidence appears. The selected target primitives then provide box prompts and temporal support for video mask prediction. We construct TCoVP-SFT-15k and TCoVP-RL-13k to learn this representation through supervised fine-tuning and chain-aligned reinforcement learning. Extensive experiments across five VRS benchmarks and three model backbones demonstrate the strong performance of TCoVP, highlighting the effectiveness of organizing spatial and temporal evidence within the reasoning process. All models and code will be publicly released. Project page: \url{https://victor-wjw.github.io/TCoVP/}

papers.title_en: A 3D-Driven Framework for Moving-Camera Perspective-to-360° Video Generation
papers.authors: Michael Wakeham, Mrinmoy Kumar Das, Wenqi Wang, Ayush Tewari, Boqing Gong, Deepti Ghadiyaram
papers.evidence: 三维驱动模块化框架将透视视频与共享场景表示融合
papers.tldr: 将移动相机透视视频转为360°视频，需同时保留已观测内容、补全未见区域，并在视角变化中保持场景一致。现有方法通常让单一条件视频模型联合学习这些要求。本文提出模块化3D驱动框架，用共享场景表示连接显式3D重建、全景图像补全和生成内容回投。在Argus静态场景子集上无需全景视频训练即取得保真、感知质量和几何一致性最优。
papers.abstract_en: Turning a moving-camera perspective video into a 360° video requires more than just generating content outside the input frame: observations revealed over time must be preserved, unseen regions completed, and the resulting scene kept consistent as the camera viewpoint changes. Existing methods assign these different requirements to a single conditional video model, requiring them to be jointly learned from panoramic video data. We instead present a modular, 3D-driven framework that distributes these three responsibilities across specialized components, all connected through a shared scene representation. Input observations are reconstructed explicitly in 3D, while a pretrained panoramic image model completes unobserved content from a selected panoramic render. This generated content is lifted into the shared 3D scene, where it remains spatially anchored across camera viewpoints. Without requiring any additional panoramic-video training, our framework achieves state-of-the-art input-view fidelity, perceptual quality, and geometric consistency on a static-scene subset of the Argus evaluation set. These results support our decomposed, 3D-driven formulation as a promising alternative to direct video generation in this setting.

papers.title_en: EchoNav: Evidential BEV Completion from Historical Observations for Visual Navigation
papers.authors: Diwen Liu, Yiyang Shao, Borui Wang, Chi Zhang, Yunhui Liu
papers.evidence: 通过时序聚合与历史BEV补全恢复曾观测结构
papers.tldr: 针对杂乱环境视觉导航中遮挡结构与自由空间难恢复的问题，EchoNav 从短 RGB 序列预测证据化 BEV 占据地图。方法融合冻结 VGGT-Omega 特征与历史残差提案，用逐单元权重和学习式不更新选项完成时序聚合与占据补全，且无需深度、相机位姿或显式几何变换。仿真双目标导航成功率达 89.6%，较最强基线高 32.5 个百分点；轮式机器人 60 次试验成功率为 73.3%。
papers.abstract_en: Visual navigation in cluttered environments requires robots to recover previously observed structure and infer obstacles and free space that remain occluded. We present a framework that combines temporal aggregation and occupancy completion in an evidential bird's-eye-view (BEV) representation predicted from short RGB sequences. A decoder adapts frozen VGGT-Omega features and combines historical residual proposals using cellwise weights and a learned no-update option. The BEV predictor produces a local map in the latest ego frame without depth or camera-pose inputs or explicit geometric warping. The evidential model treats observed free space separately and predicts occupancy with associated confidence across the remaining supported region. We train the predictor on simulated RGB sequences paired with complete and visibility-masked occupancy annotations. Our experiments evaluate navigation in simulation and on a wheeled robot, with additional demonstrations on quadruped and humanoid robots. In simulated sequential two-goal navigation, our system achieves 89.6% success, outperforming the strongest evaluated baseline by 32.5 percentage points. Across 60 wheeled-robot trials in 20 scenes, it achieves 73.3% success, compared with 33.3% for the strongest evaluated baseline.

papers.title_en: CatchUp: Depth-Aware Re-Admission of Visual Tokens for Efficient Large Vision-Language Models
papers.evidence: 大视觉语言模型中深度感知的视觉token保留与再接纳
papers.tldr: 大型视觉语言模型在各解码层反复处理数百个视觉token，现有推理期剪枝常不可逆丢弃低秩token，但高关注token会随深度变化。CatchUp是免训练的深度感知视觉token重准入框架：按区间重评估查询相关性，仅处理选中token，并用相关token的参考到当前转移信号近似遗漏的表示演化。在指代表达定位与六项多模态基准上，64/128/192 token预算均获最高平均相对保留；64 token时活跃视觉token减少88.9%，六项基准平均保留92.17%全模型性能，端到端延迟降低8.0%。
papers.abstract_en: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) repeatedly process hundreds of visual tokens across decoder layers, incurring substantial computation and memory costs. Existing inference-time visual token pruning methods often irreversibly remove low-ranked tokens, although the set of visual tokens receiving high query-conditioned attention can change across decoder depth. Recoverable routing preserves skipped tokens for later reconsideration, but re-admits them with stale representations after bypassing intermediate transformations. We further find that replacing stale re-admitted states with their current-depth oracle states from a full-token reference trajectory substantially improves grounding performance. We therefore propose CatchUp, a training-free framework for depth-aware visual-token re-admission. CatchUp repeatedly re-evaluates query-conditioned visual relevance, processes only selected visual tokens through each decoder interval, and preserves deferred tokens for later re-admission. Upon re-admission, CatchUp approximates missed representation evolution using reference-to-current transition signals from semantically and spatially related visual tokens. Across three referring-expression grounding datasets and six multimodal benchmarks, CatchUp achieves the highest average relative retention in both benchmark groups at 64-, 128-, and 192-token budgets. At a 64-token budget with 88.9% fewer active visual tokens, CatchUp retains 92.17% of the full model's performance on average across six multimodal benchmarks while reducing end-to-end latency by 8.0%. Code is available at https://github.com/pej0918/CatchUp

papers.title_en: Hierarchical and Query-Aware Visual Token Pruning for High-Resolution LVLMs
papers.authors: Luther Wei, Ling Zou, Kang-Yang Huang, Yu-Syuan Xu, Wen-Huang Cheng
papers.evidence: 查询感知的分层令牌剪枝压缩高分辨率LVLM视觉令牌
papers.tldr: 高分辨率LVLM通过全局缩略图与局部裁剪保留细节，但数千视觉token使LLM推理成为瓶颈。本文提出免训练的分层查询感知剪枝框架，在进入LLM前按实例、裁剪、token三级分配预算并融合查询与视觉显著性选择关键token。在LLaVA-NeXT-7B上，保留25%和10%视觉token时分别维持98.0%和94.8%性能，25%保留下吞吐提升2.0倍。该即插即用方法显著降低高分辨率LVLM推理成本。
papers.abstract_en: High-resolution Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) preserve critical, fine-grained visual details by encoding a global thumbnail alongside multiple local crops. However, the resulting thousands of vision tokens introduce severe computational bottlenecks during Large Language Model (LLM) inference. Existing token pruning methods rely primarily on query-agnostic visual saliency, while current query-aware approaches either operate at a coarse crop-level resolution or compute token relevance too late, after vision tokens have already entered the heavy LLM layers. To address this, we propose a training-free, hierarchical token pruning framework that utilizes query guidance prior to executing any LLM blocks. Our top-down hierarchy first operates at the instance-level, dynamically scaling the vision token retention ratio of each sample based on its visual complexity. Next, at the crop-level, we distribute this sample budget across local crops using sentence-level cross-modal similarity. Finally, at the token-level, we exploit projected vision tokens alongside textual query token embeddings in the shared space to measure fine-grained alignment, applying a text-debiasing normalization to produce high-fidelity query scores. These query-guided budgets and scores are fused with local and global visual saliency metrics to select the most critical vision tokens. Extensive experiments on LLaVA-NeXT-7B demonstrate that our plug-and-play framework retains 98.0% and 94.8% of unpruned performance at 25% and 10% vision token retention, respectively. Notably, at 25% retention, our method delivers a 2.0x inference throughput speedup and even surpasses the unpruned baseline on POPE by 0.7 points.

papers.title_en: DiffGround: Semantic Difference-Guided Zero-Shot Video Question Grounding
papers.authors: Cheng-Han Lee, Amir Salimi, Hsiang-Wei Huang, Che-Chun Su, Min Sun, Cheng-Hao Kuo
papers.evidence: 视觉-语言模型依据动作线索检索查询选取关键帧
papers.tldr: 视频问答定位需同时准确答题与精确定位时间段，但监督方法依赖昂贵时序标注，现有零样本方法多面向VQA而未针对定位优化。本文提出DiffGround，基于冻结多模态大模型，先预测与答案相关的动作线索，将问题转为显式定位目标，并引导VLM选取关键帧推理，再用语义差异精化从稀疏预测恢复完整动作片段。在NExT-GQA和STAR上一致超越零样本与监督方法，刷新该任务最优结果。
papers.abstract_en: Video Question Grounding (VideoQG) requires both accurate question answering and precise temporal localization. Existing supervised methods rely on costly temporal annotations, while existing zero-shot approaches are primarily designed for Video Question Answering (VQA) and are not optimized for temporal grounding. We propose DiffGround, an action-driven zero-shot framework built upon frozen Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). Our framework first predicts an answer-relevant action cue that transforms the input question into an explicit semantic target for grounding. Action Cue converts a reasoningoriented question into an action-centric retrieval query. Guided by the action cue, a Vision-Language Model (VLM) efficiently selects informative keyframes for reasoning. Finally, we introduce Semantic Diff Refinement, a training-free temporal refinement method that exploits semantic differences between neighboring SigLIP2 embeddings to recover complete action segments from sparse predictions. Extensive experiments on NExT-GQA and STAR show that DiffGround consistently outperforms existing zero-shot and supervised methods, establishing a new state of the art for Video Question Grounding.

papers.title_en: Policy-Adaptive Credit Assignment for Spatial Reasoning with Verifiable Rewards
papers.evidence: 面向图像空间推理各阶段的自适应过程奖励
papers.tldr: 图像空间推理需感知、分解与推断，瓶颈阶段会随训练变化；答案级奖励难以定位失败阶段，固定过程权重也无法适配。CALIPER利用SpatialTrace的分阶段轨迹，通过组内岭回归估计各阶段覆盖与答案正确性的关联，并动态更新过程奖励权重。在八个基准和三个骨干上，其一次性与闭环训练平均表现均最佳，优于固定分配。该工作实现了策略自适应的信用分配。
papers.abstract_en: Image-based spatial reasoning requires perception, decomposition, and inference, but the stage that limits accuracy can change during training. Answer-level rewards neither localize failures to individual stages nor provide discriminative group-relative feedback when all rollouts receive the same reward. Process supervision provides intermediate feedback, but fixed weights cannot adapt reward allocation to these changing bottlenecks. To address this gap, we propose CALIPER, an adaptive process-reward framework supported by SpatialTrace, a corpus of stage-decomposed spatial reasoning traces. CALIPER jointly estimates the associations between stage-wise reference coverage and answer correctness through within-group ridge regression, using these associations as utility proxies to gradually update reward weights. The resulting process reward supervises all rollout groups, including uniformly failing ones. Because utility estimates can become unreliable when answer-discriminative groups are scarce, a closed-loop harness monitors estimator reliability and validation performance to guide checkpoint rollback, rollout diversification, and early stopping. Extensive experiments across eight benchmarks and three backbones show that CALIPER achieves the highest mean under both one-shot and harness training, with consistent gains over fixed allocation across RL optimizers. Further analyses confirm the benefits of adaptive reward allocation and harness control, with favorable scaling in model/data size.

papers.title_en: PointForward V2: Point-Aligned Interaction for Feedforward Driving Reconstruction
papers.authors: Xianqi Wang, Cheng Chi, Yuechuan Pu, Hongcheng Luo, Junda Cheng, Guang Chen, Hangjun Ye, Bing Wang, Xin Yang
papers.evidence: 多视角时序融合为三维点表示
papers.tldr: 动态驾驶场景的前馈重建需融合多视角多时刻观测，但现有点查询大多独立处理，全局注意力计算代价高。PointForward V2 提出以场景结构化寄存器作为中介，实现点对齐交互：静态背景用逐帧寄存器跨帧通信，动态实例在规范空间内经实例寄存器交互，并结合4D位置编码。方法在Waymo、nuScenes和Argoverse 2上取得领先性能。该工作将点对齐表示推进为可扩展的时空交互，提升前馈驾驶重建能力。
papers.abstract_en: Feedforward reconstruction of dynamic driving scenes requires integrating observations across multiple views and time steps into a coherent 3D representation. PointForward established state-of-the-art feedforward driving reconstruction by lifting image observations into sparse 3D queries, demonstrating the effectiveness of point-aligned scene representations. However, these queries are largely processed independently, limiting information exchange across space and time, while direct global attention among tens of thousands of point queries is computationally prohibitive. In this work, we present \textbf{PointForward V2}, which advances point-aligned representation to point-aligned interaction. Our key idea is to mediate query interaction through compact, scene-structured registers. For the static background, frame-wise Static Scene Registers compress point information, communicate across frames, and propagate the aggregated context back to the queries. For each dynamic instance, queries from different frames are aligned in an object-centric canonical space and interact through instance-specific Dynamic Instance Registers. We further employ 4D positional encoding that combines aligned spatial coordinates with original timestamps, enabling spatially aligned yet temporally distinguishable interactions. In this way, PointForward V2 enables scalable spatio-temporal reasoning directly among lifted 3D queries without dense global attention. Experiments on Waymo, nuScenes, and Argoverse 2 demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across large-scale driving benchmarks.
